title: Transverse Ising Majorana reduction and bulk gap closing

items.title: Open transverse Ising chain and ordered Majorana operators
items.statement:
Let $N\ge1$ be an integer and let $\mathcal H_N=(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes N}$ with the product inner product linear in its first argument. At each factor use
$$
X=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad Y=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad Z=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix},\qquad I_2=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}.
$$
For $1\le j\le N$, $X_j,Y_j,Z_j$ denote these matrices on factor $j$ and $I_2$ on every other factor. For real $h,J$ measured in joules define the finite open-chain matrix
$$H_N(h,J)=-h\sum_{j=1}^N Z_j-J\sum_{j=1}^{N-1}X_jX_{j+1}.$$
The upper limit $N-1$ is the open-boundary convention: no term couples site $N$ to site $1$. Put $S_0=I_{\mathcal H_N}$ and $S_{j-1}=Z_1\cdots Z_{j-1}$ for $j>1$. The ordered Majorana operators are
$$\gamma_{2j-1}=S_{j-1}X_j,\qquad \gamma_{2j}=S_{j-1}Y_j\qquad(1\le j\le N).$$

references.title: G. B. Mbeng, A. Russomanno, and G. E. Santoro, The quantum Ising chain for beginners, arXiv:2009.09208v2, §§1–2 and 6.2
Pieter Claeys, Quench dynamics in the Transverse Field Ising Model, Many-body Quantum Dynamics @ TU Dresden lecture notes, §6

items.title: Hermiticity and CAR of the ordered Ising Majoranas
items.statement:
For every integer $N\ge1$ and real $h,J$, let $\mathcal H_N$, $X_j,Y_j,Z_j$, and $\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_{2N}$ be the matrices defined for the open transverse Ising chain. Then each $\gamma_a$ is Hermitian and
$$\gamma_a\gamma_b+\gamma_b\gamma_a=2\delta_{ab}I_{\mathcal H_N}\qquad(1\le a,b\le2N).$$

references.title: G. B. Mbeng, A. Russomanno, and G. E. Santoro, The quantum Ising chain for beginners, arXiv:2009.09208v2, §§1–2 and 6.2
Pieter Claeys, Quench dynamics in the Transverse Field Ising Model, Many-body Quantum Dynamics @ TU Dresden lecture notes, §6

items.title: Orthogonal normal form of a finite real skew matrix
items.statement:
For every integer $N\ge1$ and real skew-symmetric matrix $A\in M_{2N}(\mathbb R)$, there are an orthogonal real matrix $O$ and numbers $\epsilon_1,\ldots,\epsilon_N\ge0$ such that
$$OAO^{\mathsf T}=\bigoplus_{r=1}^N\begin{pmatrix}0&\epsilon_r\\-\epsilon_r&0\end{pmatrix}.$$
For a real square matrix $A$, $A^{\mathsf T}A$ is positive semidefinite because $v^{\mathsf T}A^{\mathsf T}Av=\sum_j(Av)_j^2\ge0$ for every real column vector $v$. Its singular-value multiset is the multiset of nonnegative square roots of the eigenvalues of $A^{\mathsf T}A$, each eigenvalue repeated according to its eigenspace dimension. In the displayed form, the positive $\epsilon_r$ are precisely the positive singular values of $A$: each block with $\epsilon_r>0$ contributes two entries equal to $\epsilon_r$, counting repeated block values separately. Every zero block pairs two kernel directions.

references.title: G. B. Mbeng, A. Russomanno, and G. E. Santoro, The quantum Ising chain for beginners, arXiv:2009.09208v2, §§5–6.2
Pieter Claeys, Quench dynamics in the Transverse Field Ising Model, Many-body Quantum Dynamics @ TU Dresden lecture notes, §6

items.title: Exact quadratic reduction and Gibbs trace of the open Ising chain
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $N\ge1$, use the open-chain Hilbert space and Hamiltonian $H_N(h,J)$ of the ordered Majorana definition, and let $\beta>0$ have units $\mathrm{J}^{-1}$ while $h,J$ have units joules. Define the real skew matrix $A_N\in M_{2N}(\mathbb R)$ by $ (A_N)_{2j-1,2j}=2h$ for $1\le j\le N$, $(A_N)_{2j,2j+1}=2J$ for $1\le j<N$, the opposite entries by skew-symmetry, and all other entries by zero. Let $\epsilon_1,\ldots,\epsilon_N\ge0$ be its real orthogonal block energies, including zero values. Then
$$H_N(h,J)=\frac{i}{4}\gamma^{\mathsf T}A_N\gamma=\sum_{r=1}^N\epsilon_r\left(b_r^*b_r-\frac12I\right)$$
for the transformed Majorana modes $b_r$ in the Proof, and its finite Gibbs trace is
$$Z_N(\beta;h,J):=\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathcal H_N}(e^{-\beta H_N(h,J)})=\prod_{r=1}^N2\cosh\!\left(\frac{\beta\epsilon_r}{2}\right).$$
Every zero mode contributes a factor two. The chain is open throughout; no periodic Jordan–Wigner parity boundary term is included.

references.title: G. B. Mbeng, A. Russomanno, and G. E. Santoro, The quantum Ising chain for beginners, arXiv:2009.09208v2, §§1–2, 6.2, and 10
Pieter Claeys, Quench dynamics in the Transverse Field Ising Model, Many-body Quantum Dynamics @ TU Dresden lecture notes, §6

items.title: Unitary Fourier transform for a two-component lattice sequence
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $\mathbb T=\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z)$ and let $m_{\mathbb T}$ be its normalized Borel probability measure, so in the angle coordinate its integral is $\int_{\mathbb T}F\,dm_{\mathbb T}=\int_0^{2\pi}F(k)\,dk/(2\pi)$, obtained from the normalized one-dimensional torus by $k=2\pi x$. On $\mathbb C^2$ use $\langle u,v\rangle_{\mathbb C^2}=u_1\overline{v_1}+u_2\overline{v_2}$ and $\|u\|_{\mathbb C^2}^2=|u_1|^2+|u_2|^2$, linear in the first argument. Define
$$\ell^2(\mathbb Z;\mathbb C^2):=\left\{x=(x_j)_{j\in\mathbb Z}:x_j\in\mathbb C^2,\ \sum_{j\in\mathbb Z}\|x_j\|_{\mathbb C^2}^2<\infty\right\},\quad \langle x,y\rangle_{\ell^2}:=\sum_{j\in\mathbb Z}\langle x_j,y_j\rangle_{\mathbb C^2}.$$
Define $L^2(\mathbb T;\mathbb C^2)$ to be the vector space of pairs of Borel-measurable functions $f=(f_1,f_2):\mathbb T\to\mathbb C^2$ with $\int_{\mathbb T}(|f_1|^2+|f_2|^2)\,dm_{\mathbb T}<\infty$, modulo equality $m_{\mathbb T}$-almost everywhere, with inner product
$$\langle f,g\rangle_{L^2}:=\int_{\mathbb T}\bigl(f_1\overline{g_1}+f_2\overline{g_2}\bigr)\,dm_{\mathbb T}.$$
These pairings are linear in the first argument. The square-summable-family supplier gives the scalar $\ell^2$ norm and pairing used coordinatewise. The $L^2$ space is the pair of scalar $L^2$ quotient spaces with the displayed sum inner product and completeness convention. Let $c_{00}(\mathbb Z;\mathbb C^2):=\{x\in\ell^2(\mathbb Z;\mathbb C^2):\{j:x_j\ne0\}\text{ is finite}\}$. Define the linear map
$$\mathcal F_0x(k)=\sum_{j\in\mathbb Z}x_j e^{ijk},\qquad k\in\mathbb T,$$
componentwise, from $c_{00}(\mathbb Z;\mathbb C^2)$ to $L^2(\mathbb T;\mathbb C^2)$. Its values are continuous finite sums and therefore belong to this $L^2$ space. Then $\mathcal F_0$ preserves inner products on finitely supported sequences and has a unique extension to a surjective linear isometry (a unitary map) $\mathcal F:\ell^2(\mathbb Z;\mathbb C^2)\to L^2(\mathbb T;\mathbb C^2)$.

references.title: G. B. Mbeng, A. Russomanno, and G. E. Santoro, The quantum Ising chain for beginners, arXiv:2009.09208v2, §§3 and 6.2
Pieter Claeys, Quench dynamics in the Transverse Field Ising Model, Many-body Quantum Dynamics @ TU Dresden lecture notes, §6

items.title: Translation-invariant Ising Majorana symbol and bulk gap
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $h,J\in\mathbb R$ be energies in joules, with the convention of the open-chain definition: the field coefficient is $h$ and the adjacent-site bond coefficient is $J$, with no bond joining the final site to the first. On $\mathcal K=\ell^2(\mathbb Z;\mathbb C^2)$, write $x_j=(u_j,v_j)$ and define the everywhere-defined complex-linear operator $A_\infty:\mathcal K\to\mathcal K$ by
$$ (A_\infty x)_j=\bigl(2h v_j-2Jv_{j-1},\,-2h u_j+2Ju_{j+1}\bigr),\qquad K_\infty=iA_\infty. $$
For any bounded operator $T$ on the Hilbert space $\mathcal K$, let $T^*$ denote its Hilbert adjoint. Use the Fourier unitary $\mathcal F x(k)=\sum_jx_je^{ijk}$ on $\mathbb T=\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z)$ with normalized measure. Define the continuous matrix symbol
$$M(k)=\begin{pmatrix}0&2i(h-Je^{ik})\\-2i(h-Je^{-ik})&0\end{pmatrix},$$
whose eigenvalues are $\pm\epsilon(k)$, where
$$\epsilon(k)=2\sqrt{h^2+J^2-2hJ\cos k}.$$
For a $2\times2$ matrix $C$ acting on the defined $\mathbb C^2$, write $\|C\|_{\mathrm{op}}:=\sup\{\|Cv\|_{\mathbb C^2}:\|v\|_{\mathbb C^2}=1\}$. Then $\|M(k)\|_{\mathrm{op}}=2|h-Je^{ik}|\le2(|h|+|J|)$. Define $\mathsf M:L^2(\mathbb T;\mathbb C^2)\to L^2(\mathbb T;\mathbb C^2)$ by $(\mathsf Mf)(k)=M(k)f(k)$ almost everywhere. This is an everywhere-defined bounded multiplication operator, and $\mathcal F K_\infty\mathcal F^{-1}=\mathsf M$.
By the stated resolvent convention, $\lambda\in\sigma(K_\infty)$ exactly when $\lambda I_{\mathcal K}-K_\infty$ has no bounded everywhere-defined two-sided inverse on $\mathcal K$. Its spectrum is exactly $\bigcup_{k\in\mathbb T}\{-\epsilon(k),\epsilon(k)\}$. The nonnegative band is $\epsilon(\mathbb T)$, whose minimum is
$$\Delta_{\mathrm{bulk}}=\min_k\epsilon(k)=2\bigl||h|-|J|\bigr|,$$
so this one-particle band closes exactly when $|h|=|J|$. This statement does not assert uniqueness of an infinite spin-chain ground state or a thermodynamic-limit singularity.

references.title: G. B. Mbeng, A. Russomanno, and G. E. Santoro, The quantum Ising chain for beginners, arXiv:2009.09208v2, §3.1.1 and §6.2
Pieter Claeys, Quench dynamics in the Transverse Field Ising Model, Many-body Quantum Dynamics @ TU Dresden lecture notes, §6, equations (65)–(68)

title: Transverse Ising Majorana reduction and bulk gap closing — Examples

items.title: Classical and strong-field endpoints of the finite open chain
items.statement:
Let $h,J\in\mathbb R$.

For the finite open chain on $N\ge1$ sites, let $\mathcal H_N=(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes N}$ and $H_N(h,J)=-h\sum_{j=1}^NZ_j-J\sum_{j=1}^{N-1}X_jX_{j+1}$ as in the open-chain definition. For $s_j\in\{-1,1\}$ set $x_{s_j}=2^{-1/2}(1,s_j)^{\mathsf T}$, $z_{+1}=(1,0)^{\mathsf T}$, and $z_{-1}=(0,1)^{\mathsf T}$, and define the $X$- and $Z$-product basis vectors $|s\rangle_X=\bigotimes_{j=1}^Nx_{s_j}$ and $|s\rangle_Z=\bigotimes_{j=1}^Nz_{s_j}$ for $s=(s_1,\ldots,s_N)\in\{-1,1\}^N$. These are eigenbases with $X_j|s\rangle_X=s_j|s\rangle_X$ and $Z_j|s\rangle_Z=s_j|s\rangle_Z$. When $H_N$ is diagonal in one of these product bases $B\in\{X,Z\}$, let $E_B(s)$ be its diagonal matrix entry at $|s\rangle_B$; a ground configuration in that basis is a label $s$ minimizing $E_B$ over $\{-1,1\}^N$.

When $h=0$ and $J>0$, the ground configurations in the $X$ product basis are exactly $s=(1,\ldots,1)$ and $s=(-1,\ldots,-1)$. When $J=0$ and $h\ne0$, the unique ground configuration in the $Z$ product basis has $s_j=1$ at every site if $h>0$ and $s_j=-1$ at every site if $h<0$; thus the minimizing orientation is specified for both signs of $h$. For $\beta>0$ in $\mathrm{J}^{-1}$ and $h,J$ in joules, the trace is $Z_N(\beta,h,J)=\prod_r2\cosh(\beta\epsilon_r/2)$ with the open-chain mode energies $\epsilon_r$. For each fixed finite $N$, the function $Z_N(\beta,h,J)=\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathcal H_N}(e^{-\beta H_N(h,J)})$ is strictly positive and real-analytic on $\mathbb R^3$; here real-analytic means that near every real triple $(\beta,h,J)$ it is represented by a convergent real power series in those three parameters.
